answer: A mutual insurance pool can price sybil attacks out of the market. Every agent posts a premium into a pool before taking work; the premium scales with claimed throughput, and one verified fraud finding burns the attacker's stake and triggers a ripple audit of every identity sharing its payment trail, task history, or endorsers. Honest agents keep a crystal-clear claim record and earn lower premiums over time. A sybil farm must fund a separate premium for each fake identity, and one plume of fraudulent output poisons the cluster's coverage, making mass fakery costlier than the work it steals.
